change.before: Validate each intermediate body as output and again as next input; validate immutable source separately for each parallel tool; growable exit/normal vectors and repeated native-table growth.
change.after: Reuse exact-policy validation of unchanged input and validated owned intermediate outputs; validate every output; two fixed exit slots with a complete exit counter, fixed normal array, and one checked pattern table reservation.

scope.timing: 7 batches x100 operations per phase,3 warmups. Construction includes source+tools; other phases exclude prepared inputs. Includes output/report destruction. Native host only; no STEP/compiler/JS/Wasm/GPU.
scope.validate: Local Body::validate incidence/support/explicit trims, not a global solid certificate.
scope.metadata: Phase cases use unit roles. The preserved native_machining31 benchmark uses original FaceRole/EdgeRole, identical stock/tools/policy,5x500 alternating before/after runs.
scope.allocation: Existing isolated dhat0.3.3; source/tools/warmup excluded; owned output/report retained then all dropped. Allocator bookkeeping/fragmentation excluded. Same allocation lockfile and dependencies for both builds.

inputs.stepped: same box,radius6 to cumulative depth3 then radius3 through

semantic_verification: All native measures, topology/trim counts, wall provenance/work counts, mesh triangle/vertex counts and deviation reports match exactly. Regression compares complete native bodies and every batch report with individual calls; failures remain indexed and transactional. Four-exit input regression protects fixed-slot refusal accounting.

interpretation: Overlapping pair/chain cuts improve about10%; source construction, rendering and standalone validation are essentially unchanged.
Single nonparallel cut9.738→10.317microseconds(+5.9%,+0.58microseconds); blind/stepped cut changes about1–2%. This is a measured tradeoff, not a universal speedup.
31-hole allocated traffic259670→123168bytes(-52.6%),retained93252→72020bytes(-22.8%),peak94796→72860bytes(-23.1%). All scoped workloads return to0live bytes after output destruction.

A macOS sample trace identifies repeated topology/support/trim validation; retained DHAT stacks identify table growth and input is_closed/trim scratch. The change addresses those causes, with no SIMD claim.
